maya: Heads-up — after the canary of dynamic kernel-steering + KV-coalesce landed on staging, our structured-output eval (table parsing) shows regressions for the int4+fp8 mix. Putting findings here so we can triage.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout to staging completed at 2319876400 :rocket:

sam: ugh. which model/sequence lengths?

maya: model=redwood-rlhf-v2-mix, seqs=2k-8k tokens, typical prompt: long multi-section policy doc -> structured CSV/table extraction.

eli: can you paste the eval delta?

maya: short summary: +6.2% token-level exact-match loss on structured fields, hallucination index up from 0.7 to 2.1 per 1k tokens. Perf-wise throughput improved ~12% on p4d when batching aggressive, but latency tail increased for 99p on >4k seqs.

zoe: interesting trade. do we have profiler traces for kernel selection?

maya: yes — attaching snippets from perf run (staging, sample request):
```
SCHED_DECISION: dynamic_steer -> selected kernels: [fp8-gemm-v2, int4-attn-fused]
KV_CACHE: coalesce=true -> merged 3x small KV writes into single D2H op
LATENCY: p50=86ms p90=210ms p99=1.2s (baseline p99=900ms)
CPU: batching_thread blocked 28ms awaiting KV flush
GPU: small increase in SM occupancy, but more frequent kernel switches (avg 4->7 per token)
```

sam: that KV flush blocking sounds suspect. coalesce should reduce host ops, not add delays. Is it waiting for calibration flush?

maya: looks like we introduced a sync point when coalescing writes across micro-batches. In the code we do: `kv_coalesce_flush()` with `cudaStreamSynchronize()` if `cross_block=true`.

eli: can you point to commit?

maya: staging diff: `runtime/scheduler/kv_coalesce.cpp` commit 9f3b. Patch uses cross-block aggregation to reduce PCIe ops. Might be harmless for short seqs but for long sequences it groups pending KV writes and forces sync before next kernel.

tomas: also the kernel steering changed: we started preferring fused int4 attention kernels for memory savings, but those have different numerical ordering/accumulation which can increase sensitivity post-calibration. Combined with delayed KV availability we may be getting stale KV data into fused kernels -> output drift.

zoe: can we reproduce with `REDWOOD_DEBUG_KERNELS=1` and `REDWOOD_KV_COALESCE=0/1` toggles?

maya: yes, quick A/B runs show:
```
A: kv_coalesce=0 + legacy kernels -> EM loss baseline
B: kv_coalesce=1 + new steering -> 6.2% delta
C: kv_coalesce=1 + steering but force-kernel=fallback -> delta reduced to 1.1%
```

sam: so hypothesis: combination of kernel numeric differences + KV timing changes cause structured output breakage. Is calibration different for int4 path?

eli: calibration profiles were generated per-layer but we switched to per-shard calibration for speed; that changed scale/zero offsets slightly. That can amplify numeric differences for low-bit kernels.

maya: right — calib diff: mean scale change ~0.8% on attention proj, but rounding in int4 makes it noisy. When fused kernels reorder ops, rounding error propagates more badly for delicate structured output tokens.

tomas: actionable triage plan: 1) revert the cross-block sync in coalesce (make flush async), 2) rerun calibration with per-layer fallback for attention proj, 3) add unit tests for structured CSV/JSON outputs under mix-quant combos.

zoe: I can take (3) and create a small eval harness to run nightly.

sam: i'll prototype reverting sync to async and run perf+eval on staging. If perf improves without quality loss we keep it.

eli: i'll regenerate calib with per-layer for the attention modules and create a diff tool to compare scale/zero deltas >0.2%.

maya: temporary mitigation: pin canary to `steer=legacy-kernel` for customers and mark the mixed-quant rollout paused.

deploy-bot: Rollback flag set for canary at 2319876550 by @sam :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks. please post quick numbers after the revert test. Also add a telemetry check to detect sudden clustering of kernel-switch counts per token — that was a clear signal.

sam: will do. cc @zoe @eli for follow-ups.

zoe: adding a tiny prompt set of 250 structured examples to nightly eval now :mag_right:

eli: i'll share calib diffs in the PR. expected work ~4-6h.

maya: great. outcome goal: keep throughput gains but eliminate structured-output delta to <0.5% EM and halluc index back to <1.0 per 1k.

sam: copying notes to GitHub issue #infra/quant-triage-2319876543 and will link PRs.

maya: thanks all. feel free to ping in thread for any new logs/trace snippets.
